items.name: Loop
items.category_th: โครงสร้างโปรแกรม
items.description_en: > Reference Language | Libraries | Comparison | Changes loop() After creating a setup() function, which initializes and sets the initial values, the loop() function does precisely what its name suggests, and loops consecutively, allowing your program to change and respond. Use it to actively control the Arduino board. Example int buttonPin = 3; // setup initializes serial and the button pin void setup() { beginSerial(9600); pinMode(buttonPin, INPUT); } // loop checks the button pin each time, // and will send serial if it is pressed void loop() { if (digitalRead(buttonPin) == HIGH) serialWrite('H'); else serialWrite('L'); delay(1000); }
items.th: ส่วนที่ทำงานวนซ้ำไปเรื่อย ๆ ตลอดเวลาที่บอร์ดเปิดอยู่
items.micropython:

    led.value(1)
    time.sleep(1)
    led.value(0)
    time.sleep(1)
items.note_th: ใช้ while True: แทน loop() และโค้ดข้างในต้องย่อหน้า 4 ช่องเท่ากันทุกบรรทัด

items.name: setup()
items.category_th: โครงสร้างโปรแกรม
items.description_en: The setup() function is called when a sketch starts. Use it to initialize variables, pin modes, start using libraries, etc. The setup function will only run once, after each powerup or reset of the Arduino board. Example int buttonPin = 3; void setup() { Serial.begin(9600); pinMode(buttonPin, INPUT); } void loop() { // ... }

items.description_en: The continue statement skips the rest of the current iteration of a loop (do, for, or while). It continues by checking the conditional expression of the loop, and proceeding with any subsequent iterations.

items.name: do - while
items.category_th: คำสั่งควบคุม
items.description_en: The do loop works in the same manner as the while loop, with the exception that the condition is tested at the end of the loop, so the do loop will always run at least once. do { // statement block } while (test condition);

items.name: for statements
items.category_th: คำสั่งควบคุม
items.description_en: The for statement is used to repeat a block of statements enclosed in curly braces. An increment counter is usually used to increment and terminate the loop. The for statement is useful for any repetitive operation, and is often used in combination with arrays to operate on collections of data/pins. There are three parts to the for loop header: for (initialization; condition; increment) { //statement(s); } The initialization happens first and exactly once. Each time through the loop, the condition is tested; if it's true, the statement block, and the increment is executed, then the condition is tested again. When the condition becomes false, the loop ends.
items.th: วนทำซ้ำตามจำนวนรอบที่กำหนด
items.micropython:
for i in range(10):      # i = 0 ถึง 9
    print(i)

for b in range(0, 256, 5):   # เริ่ม 0 ถึง 255 ทีละ 5
    pwm.duty_u16(b * 257)
items.note_th: for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) เขียนเป็น for i in range(10):

items.category_th: คำสั่งควบคุม
items.description_en: if, which is used in conjunction with a comparison operator, tests whether a certain condition has been reached, such as an input being above a certain number. Put another way, if the statement in parentheses is true, the statements inside the brackets are run. If not, the program skips over the code. The brackets may be omitted after an if statement. Each test will proceed to the next one until a true test is encountered. items.description_en: #include is used to include outside libraries in your sketch. items.name: Define
items.category_th: ไวยากรณ์
items.description_en: #define is a useful C component that allows the programmer to give a name to a constant value before the program is compiled. Defined constants in arduino don't take up any program memory space on the chip. The compiler will replace references to these constants with the defined value at compile time. This can have some unwanted side effects though, if for example, a constant name that had been #defined is included in some other constant or variable name. In that case the text would be replaced by the #defined number (or text). In general, the const keyword is preferred for defining constants and should be used instead of #define. Arduino defines have the same syntax as C defines:
items.syntax:
#define constantName value
Note that the # is necessary.
items.example_cpp:
#define ledPin 3
// The compiler will replace any mention of ledPin with the value 3 at compile time.

items.name: % (modulo)
items.category_th: ตัวดำเนินการคณิตศาสตร์
items.description_en: Calculates the remainder when one integer is divided by another. It is useful for keeping a variable within a particular range (e.g. the size of an array).
items.parameters:
dividend: the number to be divided
divisor: the number to divide by
items.returns: the remainder
items.example_cpp:
x = 7 % 5;   // x now contains 2
x = 9 % 5;   // x now contains 4
x = 5 % 5;   // x now contains 0
x = 4 % 5;   // x now contains 4
items.th: หาเศษจากการหาร
items.micropython:
if count % 2 == 0:
    print('เลขคู่')
items.note_th: ใช้เหมือนกัน

items.name: = assignment operator (single equal sign)
items.category_th: ตัวดำเนินการคณิตศาสตร์
items.description_en: Stores the value to the right of the equal sign in the variable to the left of the equal sign. The single equal sign in the C programming language is called the assignment operator. It has a different meaning than in algebra class where it indicated an equation or equality. The assignment operator tells the microcontroller to evaluate whatever value or expression is on the right side of the equal sign, and store it in the variable to the left of the equal sign.
items.example_cpp:
int sensVal;                 // declare an integer variable named sensVal
 senVal = analogRead(0);       // store the (digitized) input voltage at analog pin 0 in SensVal

items.name: Addition, Subtraction, Multiplication, & Division
items.category_th: ตัวดำเนินการคณิตศาสตร์
items.description_en: These operators return the sum, difference, product, or quotient (respectively) of the two operands. The operation is conducted using the data type of the operands, so, for example, 9 / 4 gives 2 since 9 and 4 are ints. This also means that the operation can overflow if the result is larger than that which can be stored in the data type (e.g. adding 1 to an int with the value 32,767 gives -32,768). If the operands are of different types, the "larger" type is used for the calculation. If one of the numbers (operands) are of the type float or of type double, floating point math will be used for the calculation.
items.th: บวก ลบ คูณ หาร
items.micropython:
a = 7 / 2    # 3.5 (ได้ทศนิยม)
b = 7 // 2   # 3 (หารปัดเศษทิ้ง เหมือน int ใน C)
items.note_th: ใน C: 7/2 = 3 ถ้าเป็น int แต่ใน Python 7/2 = 3.5 ถ้าต้องการจำนวนเต็มให้ใช้ //

items.name: Boolean
items.category_th: ตัวดำเนินการตรรกะ
items.description_en: > Reference Language | Libraries | Comparison | Changes Boolean Operators These can be used inside the condition of an if statement. && (logical and) True only if both operands are true, e.g. if (digitalRead(2) == HIGH && digitalRead(3) == HIGH) { // read two switches // ... } is true only if both inputs are high. || (logical or) True if either operand is true, e.g. if (x > 0 || y > 0) { // ... } is true if either x or y is greater than 0. ! (not) True if the operand is false, e.g. if (!x) { // ... } is true if x is false (i.e. if x equals 0).
items.example_cpp: if (a >= 10 && a <= 20){}   // true if a is between 10 and 20

items.name: Bitwise NOT (~)
items.category_th: ตัวดำเนินการบิต
items.description_en: The bitwise NOT operator in C++ is the tilde character ~. Unlike & and |, the bitwise NOT operator is applied to a single operand to its right. Bitwise NOT changes each bit to its opposite: 0 becomes 1, and 1 becomes 0. For example: 0 1 operand1 ---------- 1 0 ~ operand1 int a = 103; // binary: 0000000001100111 int b = ~a; // binary: 1111111110011000 = -104 You might be surprised to see a negative number like -104 as the result of this operation. This is because the highest bit in an int variable is the so-called sign bit. If the highest bit is 1, the number is interpreted as negative. items.name: ++ (increment) / -- (decrement)
items.category_th: ตัวดำเนินการแบบย่อ
items.description_en: Increment or decrement a variable
items.syntax:
x++;  // increment x by one and returns the old value of x

x-- ;   // decrement x by one and returns the old value of x

items.category_th: ตัวดำเนินการแบบย่อ

items.description_en: Double precision floating point number. Occupies 4 bytes. The double implementation on the Arduino is currently exactly the same as the float, with no gain in precision.

items.name: float
items.category_th: ชนิดข้อมูล
items.description_en: Datatype for floating-point numbers, a number that has a decimal point. Floating-point numbers are often used to approximate analog and continuous values because they have greater resolution than integers. Floating-point numbers can be as large as 3.4028235E+38 and as low as -3.4028235E+38. They are stored as 32 bits (4 bytes) of information. Floats have only 6-7 decimal digits of precision. That means the total number of digits, not the number to the right of the decimal point. Unlike other platforms, where you can get more precision by using a double (e.g. up to 15 digits), on the Arduino, double is the same size as float. Floating point numbers are not exact, and may yield strange results
items.example_cpp:
float myfloat;
    float sensorCalbrate = 1.117;
items.th: ตัวเลขทศนิยม
items.micropython: volt = adc.read_u16() * 3.3 / 65535
items.note_th: ไม่ต้องบอกชนิดข้อมูล

items.name: int
items.category_th: ชนิดข้อมูล
items.description_en: Integers are your primary datatype for number storage, and store a 2 byte value. This yields a range of -32,768 to 32,767 (minimum value of -2^15 and a maximum value of (2^15) - 1). Int's store negative numbers with a technique called 2's complement math. The highest bit, sometimes refered to as the "sign" bit, flags the number as a negative number. The rest of the bits are inverted and 1 is added. The Arduino takes care of dealing with negative numbers for you, so that arithmetic operations work transparently in the expected manner. There can be an unexpected complication in dealing with the bitshift right operator (>>) however.
items.example_cpp: int ledPin = 13;
items.th: ตัวแปรจำนวนเต็ม
items.micropython: count = 0
items.note_th: ไม่ต้องบอกชนิดข้อมูล และบน Arduino Uno int เก็บได้แค่ -32768 ถึง 32767 แต่ใน MicroPython ไม่มีขีดจำกัดนี้

This page described the latter method. For more details on the String object, which gives you more functionality at the cost of more memory, see the String object page.

items.category_th: ชนิดข้อมูล
items.description_en: An unsigned data type that occupies 1 byte of memory. Same as the byte datatype. The unsigned char datatype encodes numbers from 0 to 255. For consistency of Arduino programming style, the byte data type is to be preferred.

items.name: unsigned int
items.category_th: ชนิดข้อมูล
items.description_en: Unsigned ints (unsigned integers) are the same as ints in that they store a 2 byte value. Instead of storing negative numbers however they only store positive values, yielding a useful range of 0 to 65,535 (2^16) - 1). The difference between unsigned ints and (signed) ints, lies in the way the highest bit, sometimes refered to as the "sign" bit, is interpreted. In the Arduino int type (which is signed), if the high bit is a "1", the number is interpreted as a negative number, and the other 15 bits are interpreted with 2's complement math.
items.example_cpp: unsigned int ledPin = 13;

items.name: const keyword
items.category_th: ขอบเขตตัวแปร
items.description_en: The const keyword stands for constant. It is a variable qualifier that modifies the behavior of the variable, making a variable "read-only". This means that the variable can be used just as any other variable of its type, but its value cannot be changed. You will get a compiler error if you try to assign a value to a const variable. Constants defined with the const keyword obey the rules of variable scoping that govern other variables. This, and the pitfalls of using#define, makes the const keyword a superior method for defining constants and is preferred over using #define.
items.th: ตัวแปรที่ห้ามเปลี่ยนค่า
items.micropython:
from micropython import const
LED_PIN = const(2)
items.note_th: const() ช่วยให้โค้ดเร็วขึ้นและใช้หน่วยความจำน้อยลง ใช้กับตัวเลขจำนวนเต็มเท่านั้น

items.name: Static
items.category_th: ขอบเขตตัวแปร
items.description_en: The static keyword is used to create variables that are visible to only one function. However unlike local variables that get created and destroyed every time a function is called, static variables persist beyond the function call, preserving their data between function calls. Variables declared as static will only be created and initialized the first time a function is called.
items.th: ตัวแปรในฟังก์ชันที่จำค่าเดิมไว้ข้ามการเรียก
items.micropython: count = 0   # ใช้ตัวแปรนอกฟังก์ชัน + global แทน
items.note_th: Python ไม่มี static ในฟังก์ชัน

items.name: Variable Scope
items.category_th: ขอบเขตตัวแปร
items.description_en: Variables in the C programming language, which Arduino uses, have a property called scope. This is in contrast to languages such as BASIC where every variable is a global variable. A global variable is one that can be seen by every function in a program. Local variables are only visible to the function in which they are declared. In the Arduino environment, any variable declared outside of a function (e.g. setup(), loop(), etc. ), is a global variable. When programs start to get larger and more complex, local variables are a useful way to insure that only one function has access to its own variables. This prevents programming errors when one function inadvertently modifies variables used by
items.th: ตัวแปรที่ประกาศในฟังก์ชันใช้ได้เฉพาะในฟังก์ชันนั้น
items.micropython:
count = 0

def add():
    global count
    count += 1
items.note_th: ถ้าจะแก้ตัวแปรที่ประกาศนอกฟังก์ชัน ต้องเขียน global ชื่อตัวแปร ก่อน

items.name: volatile keyword
items.category_th: ขอบเขตตัวแปร
items.description_en: volatile is a keyword known as a variable qualifier, it is usually used before the datatype of a variable, to modify the way in which the compiler and subsequent program treats the variable. Declaring a variable volatile is a directive to the compiler. The compiler is software which translates your C/C++ code into the machine code, which are the real instructions for the Atmega chip in the Arduino. Specifically, it directs the compiler to load the variable from RAM and not from a storage register, which is a temporary memory location where program variables are stored and manipulated. Under certain conditions, the value for a variable stored in registers can be inaccurate. A variable should
items.th: ตัวแปรที่ถูกเปลี่ยนในฟังก์ชันอินเทอร์รัปต์

items.name: digitalRead()
items.category_th: ขาดิจิทัล

if btn.value() == 0:   # INPUT_PULLUP: กดแล้วได้ 0

items.name: digitalWrite()
items.category_th: ขาดิจิทัล
items.description_en: Write a HIGH or a LOW value to a digital pin. If the pin has been configured as an OUTPUT with pinMode(), its voltage will be set to the corresponding value: 5V (or 3.3V on 3.3V boards) for HIGH, 0V (ground) for LOW. If the pin is configured as an INPUT, writing a HIGH value with digitalWrite() will enable an internal 20K pullup resistor (see the tutorial on digital pins). Writing LOW will disable the pullup. The pullup resistor is enough to light an LED dimly, so if LEDs appear to work, but very dimly, this is a likely cause. The remedy is to set the pin to an output with the pinMode() function. NOTE: Digital pin 13 is harder to use as a digital input than the other digital pins because it
items.parameters:
pin: the pin number
value: HIGH or LOW
items.returns: none
items.th: สั่งขาให้เป็น HIGH (มีไฟ) หรือ LOW (ไม่มีไฟ) ใช้เปิด/ปิด LED บัซเซอร์ รีเลย์
items.micropython:
led.value(1)   # HIGH
led.value(0)   # LOW
led.on(); led.off()
items.note_th: ESP32/Pico จ่ายไฟ 3.3V ไม่ใช่ 5V เหมือน Uno

items.name: pinMode()
items.category_th: ขาดิจิทัล
items.description_en: Configures the specified pin to behave either as an input or an output. See the description of digital pins for details on the functionality of the pins. As of Arduino 1.0.1, it is possible to enable the internal pullup resistors with the mode INPUT_PULLUP. Additionally, the INPUT mode explicitly disables the internal pullups.
items.parameters:
pin: the number of the pin whose mode you wish to set
mode: INPUT, OUTPUT, or INPUT_PULLUP. (see the  digital pins page for a more complete description of the functionality.)
items.returns: None
items.th: ตั้งขาเป็นขาออก (OUTPUT) หรือขาเข้า (INPUT / INPUT_PULLUP)

led = Pin(2, Pin.OUT)
btn = Pin(4, Pin.IN, Pin.PULL_UP)
items.note_th: สร้างออบเจกต์ Pin เก็บในตัวแปร แล้วใช้ตัวแปรนั้นตลอดโปรแกรม

items.name: analogRead()
items.category_th: ขาแอนะล็อก
keywords: อ่านเซนเซอร์
อ่านแอนะล็อก
items.description_en: Reads the value from the specified analog pin. The Arduino board contains a 6 channel (8 channels on the Mini and Nano, 16 on the Mega), 10-bit analog to digital converter. This means that it will map input voltages between 0 and 5 volts into integer values between 0 and 1023. This yields a resolution between readings of: 5 volts / 1024 units or, .0049 volts (4.9 mV) per unit. The input range and resolution can be changed using analogReference(). It takes about 100 microseconds (0.0001 s) to read an analog input, so the maximum reading rate is about 10,000 times a second.
items.parameters: pin: the number of the analog input pin to read from (0 to 5 on most boards, 0 to 7 on the Mini and Nano, 0 to 15 on the Mega)
items.returns: int (0 to 1023)
items.th: อ่านแรงดันจากเซนเซอร์แอนะล็อก เช่น LDR ตัวต้านทานปรับค่า ความชื้นดิน
items.micropython:
from machine import ADC, Pin
adc = ADC(Pin(34))
adc.atten(ADC.ATTN_11DB)   # ESP32: อ่านได้ถึง ~3.3V
v = adc.read_u16()          # 0 - 65535
items.note_th: Uno ได้ค่า 0-1023 แต่ read_u16() ได้ 0-65535 ถ้าต้องการเทียบกับ Uno ให้หาร 64 ขา ADC: ESP32 = 32-39 (ADC1), Pico = GP26-GP28

items.name: analogReference(type)
items.category_th: ขาแอนะล็อก
items.description_en: Configures the reference voltage used for analog input (i.e. the value used as the top of the input range). The options are: DEFAULT: the default analog reference of 5 volts (on 5V Arduino boards) or 3.3 volts (on 3.3V Arduino boards) INTERNAL: an built-in reference, equal to 1.1 volts on the ATmega168 or ATmega328 and 2.56 volts on the ATmega8 (not available on the Arduino Mega) INTERNAL1V1: a built-in 1.1V reference (Arduino Mega only) INTERNAL2V56: a built-in 2.56V reference (Arduino Mega only) EXTERNAL: the voltage applied to the AREF pin (0 to 5V only) is used as the reference.
items.parameters: type: which type of reference to use (DEFAULT, INTERNAL, INTERNAL1V1, INTERNAL2V56, or EXTERNAL).
items.returns: None.
items.th: ตั้งแรงดันอ้างอิงของการอ่านแอนะล็อก
items.micropython:
adc.atten(ADC.ATTN_11DB)   # ESP32: ช่วง 0-3.3V
adc.atten(ADC.ATTN_0DB)    # ESP32: ช่วง 0-1.1V (ละเอียดกว่า)
items.note_th: มีเฉพาะ ESP32 ส่วน Pico อ้างอิง 3.3V คงที่

items.name: analogWrite()
items.category_th: ขาแอนะล็อก
keywords: ความเร็วมอเตอร์
items.description_en: Writes an analog value (PWM wave) to a pin. Can be used to light a LED at varying brightnesses or drive a motor at various speeds. After a call to analogWrite(), the pin will generate a steady square wave of the specified duty cycle until the next call to analogWrite() (or a call to digitalRead() or digitalWrite() on the same pin). The frequency of the PWM signal is approximately 490 Hz. On most Arduino boards (those with the ATmega168 or ATmega328), this function works on pins 3, 5, 6, 9, 10, and 11. On the Arduino Mega, it works on pins 2 through 13. Older Arduino boards with an ATmega8 only support analogWrite() on pins 9, 10, and 11. You do not need to call pinMode() to set the pin as an
items.parameters:
pin: the pin to write to.
value: the duty cycle: between 0 (always off) and 255 (always on).
items.returns: nothing
items.th: ส่งสัญญาณ PWM ใช้หรี่ไฟ LED หรือปรับความเร็วมอเตอร์ ค่า 0-255
items.micropython:
from machine import PWM, Pin
pwm = PWM(Pin(2), freq=1000)
pwm.duty_u16(128 * 257)   # 128 จาก 255 = ครึ่งหนึ่ง
items.note_th: Uno ใช้ค่า 0-255 แต่ duty_u16 ใช้ 0-65535 (คูณ 257) ESP32 ใช้ PWM ได้แทบทุกขา Uno ได้เฉพาะขา ~

items.category_th: ขาเข้าออกขั้นสูง
items.description_en: Stops the generation of a square wave triggered by tone(). Has no effect if no tone is being generated. NOTE: if you want to play different pitches on multiple pins, you need to call noTone() on one pin before calling tone() on the next pin.
items.parameters: pin: the pin on which to stop generating the tone
items.returns: nothing

items.name: pulseIn()
items.category_th: ขาเข้าออกขั้นสูง
keywords: อัลตราโซนิก
items.description_en: Reads a pulse (either HIGH or LOW) on a pin. For example, if value is HIGH, pulseIn() waits for the pin to go HIGH, starts timing, then waits for the pin to go LOW and stops timing. Returns the length of the pulse in microseconds. Gives up and returns 0 if no pulse starts within a specified time out. The timing of this function has been determined empirically and will probably show errors in longer pulses. Works on pulses from 10 microseconds to 3 minutes in length.
items.parameters:
pin: the number of the pin on which you want to read the pulse.  (int)
value: type of pulse to read: either HIGH or LOW. (int)
timeout (optional): the number of microseconds to wait for the pulse to start; default is one second (unsigned long)
items.returns: the length of the pulse (in microseconds) or 0 if no pulse started before the timeout (unsigned long)
items.th: จับเวลาความยาวพัลส์เป็นไมโครวินาที ใช้กับอัลตราโซนิก HC-SR04
items.micropython:
from machine import time_pulse_us
t = time_pulse_us(echo, 1, 30000)   # รอสูงสุด 30 ms
if t > 0:
    distance_cm = t * 0.0343 / 2
items.note_th: ถ้าหมดเวลาจะได้ค่าติดลบ (Arduino ได้ 0) ให้ตรวจ t > 0 ก่อนใช้

items.name: shiftIn()
items.category_th: ขาเข้าออกขั้นสูง
items.description_en: Shifts in a byte of data one bit at a time. Starts from either the most (i.e. the leftmost) or least (rightmost) significant bit. For each bit, the clock pin is pulled high, the next bit is read from the data line, and then the clock pin is taken low. Note: this is a software implementation; Arduino also provides an SPI library that uses the hardware implementation, which is faster but only works on specific pins.
items.parameters:
dataPin: the pin on which to input each bit (int)
clockPin: the pin to toggle to signal a read from  dataPin
bitOrder: which order to shift in the bits; either MSBFIRST or LSBFIRST.
(Most Significant Bit First, or, Least Significant Bit First)
items.returns: the value read (byte)
items.th: อ่านข้อมูลทีละบิตจากไอซี 74HC165
items.micropython:
def shift_in(data_pin, clock_pin):
    v = 0
    for i in range(8):
        clock_pin.value(1)
        v = (v << 1) | data_pin.value()
        clock_pin.value(0)
    return v
items.note_th: เขียนฟังก์ชันเอง

items.name: shiftOut()
items.category_th: ขาเข้าออกขั้นสูง
items.description_en: Shifts out a byte of data one bit at a time. Starts from either the most (i.e. the leftmost) or least (rightmost) significant bit. Each bit is written in turn to a data pin, after which a clock pin is pulsed (taken high, then low) to indicate that the bit is available. Note: if you're interfacing with a device that's clocked by rising edges, you'll need to make sure that the clock pin is low before the call to shiftOut(), e.g. with a call to digitalWrite(clockPin, LOW). This is a software implementation; see also the SPI library, which provides a hardware implementation that is faster but works only on specific pins.
items.parameters:
dataPin: the pin on which to output each bit (int)
clockPin: the pin to toggle once the dataPin has been set to the correct value (int)
bitOrder: which order to shift out the bits; either MSBFIRST or LSBFIRST.
(Most Significant Bit First, or, Least Significant Bit First)
value: the data to shift out. (byte)
items.returns: None
items.th: ส่งข้อมูลทีละบิตออกไปยังไอซี 74HC595 เพื่อเพิ่มขา
items.micropython:
def shift_out(data_pin, clock_pin, value):
    for i in range(7, -1, -1):   # MSBFIRST
        data_pin.value((value >> i) & 1)
        clock_pin.value(1)
        clock_pin.value(0)
items.note_th: MicroPython ไม่มี shiftOut ให้เขียนฟังก์ชันเอง หรือใช้ SPI

items.name: tone()
items.category_th: ขาเข้าออกขั้นสูง
items.description_en: Generates a square wave of the specified frequency (and 50% duty cycle) on a pin. A duration can be specified, otherwise the wave continues until a call to noTone(). The pin can be connected to a piezo buzzer or other speaker to play tones. Only one tone can be generated at a time. If a tone is already playing on a different pin, the call to tone() will have no effect. If the tone is playing on the same pin, the call will set its frequency. items.description_en: With the Arduino Ethernet Shield, this library allows an Arduino board to connect to the internet. It can serve as either a server accepting incoming connections or a client making outgoing ones. The library supports up to four concurrent connection (incoming or outgoing or a combination). Arduino communicates with the shield using the SPI bus. This is on digital pins 11, 12, and 13 on the Uno and pins 50, 51, and 52 on the Mega. On both boards, pin 10 is used as SS. On the Mega, the hardware SS pin, 53, is not used to select the W5100, but it must be kept as an output or the SPI interface won't work.

items.description_en: Attach the Servo variable to a pin. Note that in Arduino 0016 and earlier, the Servo library supports only servos on only two pins: 9 and 10.
items.parameters:
servo: a variable of type Servo
pin: the number of the pin that the servo is attached to
min (optional): the pulse width, in microseconds, corresponding to the minimum (0-degree) angle on the servo (defaults to 544)
max (optional): the pulse width, in microseconds, corresponding to the maximum (180-degree) angle on the servo (defaults to 2400)
items.th: บอกว่าเซอร์โวต่ออยู่ที่ขาไหน
items.micropython: servo = PWM(Pin(18), freq=50)

items.name: servo.attached()
items.category_th: ไลบรารี Servo
items.description_en: Check whether the Servo variable is attached to a pin.
items.parameters: servo: a variable of type Servo
items.returns: true if the servo is attached to pin; false otherwise.

items.name: servo.detach()
items.category_th: ไลบรารี Servo
items.description_en: Detach the Servo variable from its pin. If all Servo variables are detached, then pins 9 and 10 can be used for PWM output with analogWrite().
items.parameters: servo: a variable of type Servo
items.th: เลิกส่งสัญญาณไปที่เซอร์โว
items.micropython: servo.deinit()

items.name: servo.read()
items.category_th: ไลบรารี Servo
items.description_en: Read the current angle of the servo (the value passed to the last call to write()).
items.parameters: servo: a variable of type Servo
items.returns: The angle of the servo, from 0 to 180 degrees.

items.name: servo.write()
items.category_th: ไลบรารี Servo
items.description_en: Writes a value to the servo, controlling the shaft accordingly. On a standard servo, this will set the angle of the shaft (in degrees), moving the shaft to that orientation. On a continuous rotation servo, this will set the speed of the servo (with 0 being full-speed in one direction, 180 being full speed in the other, and a value near 90 being no movement).
items.parameters:
servo: a variable of type Servo
angle: the value to write to the servo, from 0 to 180
items.th: สั่งเซอร์โวหมุนไปที่มุมที่กำหนด
items.micropython: servo_angle(90)   # ใช้ฟังก์ชัน servo_angle ด้านบน

items.name: servo.writeMicroseconds()
items.category_th: ไลบรารี Servo
items.description_en: Writes a value in microseconds (uS) to the servo, controlling the shaft accordingly. On a standard servo, this will set the angle of the shaft. On standard servos a parameter value of 1000 is fully counter-clockwise, 2000 is fully clockwise, and 1500 is in the middle. Note that some manufactures do not follow this standard very closely so that servos often respond to values between 700 and 2300. Feel free to increase these endpoints until the servo no longer continues to increase its range. Note however that attempting to drive a servo past its endpoints (often indicated by a growling sound) is a high-current state, and should be avoided. Continuous-rotation servos will respond to the writeM
items.parameters:
servo: a variable of type Servo
uS: the value of the parameter in microseconds (int)
items.th: สั่งเซอร์โวด้วยความกว้างพัลส์ (ไมโครวินาที)
items.micropython: servo.duty_ns(1500 * 1000)   # 1500 µs = กึ่งกลาง
items.note_th: duty_ns ใช้ได้บน ESP32 และ Pico

items.name: lcd.autoscroll()
items.category_th: ไลบรารีจอ LCD
items.description_en: Turns on automatic scrolling of the LCD. This causes each character output to the display to push previous characters over by one space. If the current text direction is left-to-right (the default), the display scrolls to the left; if the current direction is right-to-left, the display scrolls to the right. This has the effect of outputting each new character to the same location on the LCD.
items.parameters: lcd: a variable of type LiquidCrystal

items.name: lcd.begin()
items.category_th: ไลบรารีจอ LCD
items.description_en: Specifies the dimensions (width and height) of the display.
items.parameters:
lcd: a variable of type LiquidCrystal
cols: the number of columns that the display has
rows: the number of rows that the display has

items.name: lcd.blink()
items.category_th: ไลบรารีจอ LCD
items.description_en: Display the blinking LCD cursor. If used in combination with the cursor() function, the result will depend on the particular display.
items.parameters: lcd: a variable of type LiquidCrystal

items.name: lcd.clear()
items.category_th: ไลบรารีจอ LCD
items.description_en: Clears the LCD screen and positions the cursor in the upper-left corner.
items.parameters: lcd: a variable of type LiquidCrystal
items.th: ล้างหน้าจอ
items.micropython: lcd.clear()

items.name: lcd.createChar()
items.category_th: ไลบรารีจอ LCD
items.description_en: Create a custom character (gylph) for use on the LCD. Up to eight characters of 5x8 pixels are supported (numbered 0 to 7). The appearance of each custom character is specified by an array of eight bytes, one for each row. The five least significant bits of each byte determine the pixels in that row. To display a custom character on the screen, write() its number.
items.parameters:
lcd: a variable of type LiquidCrystal
num: which character to create (0 to 7)
data: the character's pixel data

items.name: lcd.cursor()
items.category_th: ไลบรารีจอ LCD
items.description_en: Display the LCD cursor: an underscore (line) at the position to which the next character will be written.
items.parameters: lcd: a variable of type LiquidCrystal

items.name: lcd.display()
items.category_th: ไลบรารีจอ LCD
items.description_en: Turns on the LCD display, after it's been turned off with noDisplay(). This will restore the text (and cursor) that was on the display.
items.parameters: lcd: a variable of type LiquidCrystal

items.name: lcd.home()
items.category_th: ไลบรารีจอ LCD
items.description_en: Positions the cursor in the upper-left of the LCD. That is, use that location in outputting subsequent text to the display. To also clear the display, use the clear() function instead.
items.parameters: lcd: a variable of type LiquidCrystal

items.name: lcd.leftToRight()
items.category_th: ไลบรารีจอ LCD
items.description_en: Set the direction for text written to the LCD to left-to-right, the default. This means that subsequent characters written to the display will go from left to right, but does not affect previously-output text.
items.parameters: lcd: a variable of type LiquidCrystal

items.name: lcd.LiquidCrystal()
items.category_th: ไลบรารีจอ LCD
items.description_en: Creates a variable of type LiquidCrystal. The display can be controlled using 4 or 8 data lines. If the former, omit the pin numbers for d0 to d3 and leave those lines unconnected. The RW pin can be tied to ground instead of connected to a pin on the Arduino; if so, omit it from this function's parameters.
items.syntax:
LiquidCrystal(rs, enable, d4, d5, d6, d7)
LiquidCrystal(rs, rw, enable, d4, d5, d6, d7)
LiquidCrystal(rs, enable, d0, d1, d2, d3, d4, d5, d6, d7)
LiquidCrystal(rs, rw, enable, d0, d1, d2, d3, d4, d5, d6, d7)
items.parameters:
rs: the number of the Arduino pin that is connected to the RS pin on the LCD
rw: the number of the Arduino pin that is connected to the RW pin on the LCD (optional)
enable: the number of the Arduino pin that is connected to the enable pin on the LCD
d0, d1, d2, d3, d4, d5, d6, d7: the numbers of the Arduino pins that are connected to the corresponding data pins on the LCD.  d0, d1, d2, and d3 are optional; if omitted, the LCD will be controlled using only the four data lines (d4, d5, d6, d7).

items.name: lcd.noAutoscroll()
items.category_th: ไลบรารีจอ LCD
items.description_en: Turns off automatic scrolling of the LCD.
items.parameters: lcd: a variable of type LiquidCrystal

items.name: lcd.noBlink()
items.category_th: ไลบรารีจอ LCD
items.description_en: Turns off the blinking LCD cursor.
items.parameters: lcd: a variable of type LiquidCrystal

items.name: lcd.noCursor()
items.category_th: ไลบรารีจอ LCD

items.parameters: lcd: a variable of type LiquidCrystal

items.name: lcd.noDisplay()
items.category_th: ไลบรารีจอ LCD

items.name: lcd.print()

data: the data to print (char, byte, int, long, or string)
BASE (optional): the base in which to print numbers: BIN for binary (base 2), DEC for decimal (base 10), OCT for octal (base 8), HEX for hexadecimal (base 16).
items.returns: byte print() will return the number of bytes written, though reading that number is optional
items.th: แสดงข้อความบนจอ
items.micropython: lcd.putstr('Temp: %d' % t)

items.name: lcd.rightToLeft()
items.category_th: ไลบรารีจอ LCD
items.description_en: Set the direction for text written to the LCD to right-to-left (the default is left-to-right). This means that subsequent characters written to the display will go from right to left, but does not affect previously-output text.
items.parameters: lcd: a variable of type LiquidCrystal

items.name: lcd.scrollDisplayLeft()
items.category_th: ไลบรารีจอ LCD
items.description_en: Scrolls the contents of the display (text and cursor) one space to the left.
items.parameters: lcd: a variable of type LiquidCrystal

items.name: lcd.scrollDisplayRight()

items.description_en: Scrolls the contents of the display (text and cursor) one space to the right.
items.parameters: lcd: a variable of type LiquidCrystal

items.name: lcd.setCursor()
items.category_th: ไลบรารีจอ LCD
items.description_en: Position the LCD cursor; that is, set the location at which subsequent text written to the LCD will be displayed.
items.parameters:
lcd: a variable of type LiquidCrystal
col: the column at which to position the cursor (with 0 being the first column)
row: the row at which to position the cursor (with 0 being the first row)

items.name: lcd.write()
items.category_th: ไลบรารีจอ LCD

items.parameters:

data: the character to write to the display
items.returns: byte write() will return the number of bytes written, though reading that number is optional

items.name: stepper.Stepper(steps, pin1, pin2)
items.category_th: ไลบรารีสเต็ปเปอร์
items.description_en: This function creates a new instance of the Stepper class that represents a particular stepper motor attached to your Arduino board. Use it at the top of your sketch, above setup() and loop(). The number of parameters depends on how you've wired your motor - either using two or four pins of the Arduino board.
items.parameters:
steps: the number of steps in one revolution of your motor.  If your motor gives the number of degrees per step, divide that number into 360 to get the number of steps (e.g. 360 / 3.6 gives 100 steps).  (int)
pin1, pin2: two pins that are attached to the motor (int)
pin3, pin4: optional the last two pins attached to the motor, if it's connected to four pins (int)
items.returns: A new instance of the Stepper motor class.

items.name: Stepper: setSpeed(rpms)
items.category_th: ไลบรารีสเต็ปเปอร์
items.description_en: Sets the motor speed in rotations per minute (RPMs). This function doesn't make the motor turn, just sets the speed at which it will when you call step().
items.parameters: rpms: the speed at which the motor should turn in rotations per minute - a positive number (long)
items.returns: None
items.th: ตั้งความเร็วสเต็ปเปอร์
items.micropython: # ปรับค่า time.sleep_ms() ในฟังก์ชัน stepper_turn ยิ่งน้อยยิ่งเร็ว (ขั้นต่ำประมาณ 1 ms)

items.name: Stepper: step(steps)
items.category_th: ไลบรารีสเต็ปเปอร์
items.description_en: Turns the motor a specific number of steps, at a speed determined by the most recent call to setSpeed(). This function is blocking; that is, it will wait until the motor has finished moving to pass control to the next line in your sketch. For example, if you set the speed to, say, 1 RPM and called step(100) on a 100-step motor, this function would take a full minute to run. For better control, keep the speed high and only go a few steps with each call to step().
items.parameters: steps: the number of steps to turn the motor - positive to turn one direction, negative to turn the other (int)
items.returns: None
items.th: หมุนสเต็ปเปอร์ตามจำนวนขั้น
items.micropython: stepper_turn(512)
items.note_th: ใช้ฟังก์ชันด้านบน

items.name: Wire.available()
items.category_th: ไลบรารี Wire (I2C)
items.description_en: Returns the number of bytes available for retrieval with receive(). This should be called on a master device after a call to requestFrom() or on a slave inside the onReceive() handler. available() inherits from the Stream utility class.
items.parameters: None
items.returns: The number of bytes available for reading.
items.th: จำนวนไบต์ที่อ่านได้
items.micropython: n = len(data)

items.name: Wire.begin()
items.category_th: ไลบรารี Wire (I2C)
items.description_en: Initiate the Wire library and join the I2C bus as a master or slave. This should normally be called only once.
items.parameters: address: the 7-bit slave address (optional); if not specified, join the bus as a master.
items.returns: None
items.th: เริ่มใช้ I2C
items.micropython: i2c = I2C(0, sda=Pin(21), scl=Pin(22))

items.name: Wire.beginTransmission(address)
items.category_th: ไลบรารี Wire (I2C)
items.description_en: Begin a transmission to the I2C slave device with the given address. Subsequently, queue bytes for transmission with the write() function and transmit them by calling endTransmission().
items.parameters: address: the 7-bit address of the device to transmit to
items.returns: None
items.th: เริ่มส่งข้อมูลไปอุปกรณ์ที่อยู่ที่กำหนด
items.micropython: i2c.writeto(0x3C, bytes([0x00, 0xAF]))
items.note_th: beginTransmission + write + endTransmission รวมเป็นคำสั่งเดียว writeto()

items.name: Wire.endTransmission()
items.category_th: ไลบรารี Wire (I2C)
items.description_en: Ends a transmission to a slave device that was begun by beginTransmission() and transmits the bytes that were queued by write(). As of Arduino 1.0.1, endTransmission() accepts a boolean argument changing its behavior for compatibility with certain I2C devices. If true, endTransmission() sends a stop message after transmission, releasing the I2C bus. If false, endTransmission() sends a restart message after transmission. The bus will not be released, which prevents another master device from transmitting between messages. This allows one master device to send multiple transmissions while in control. The default value is true.
items.parameters: stop : boolean. true will send a stop message, releasing the bus after transmission. false will send a restart, keeping the connection active.
items.returns: byte, which indicates the status of the transmission: 0:success 1:data too long to fit in transmit buffer 2:received NACK on transmit of address 3:received NACK on transmit of data 4:other error
items.th: จบการส่งข้อมูล I2C
items.micropython: # ไม่ต้องเขียน writeto() ส่งและจบให้เอง

items.name: Wire.onReceive(handler)
items.category_th: ไลบรารี Wire (I2C)
items.description_en: Registers a function to be called when a slave device receives a transmission from a master.
items.parameters: handler: the function to be called when the slave receives data; this should take a single int parameter (the number of bytes read from the master) and return nothing, e.g.:  void myHandler(int numBytes)
items.returns: None

items.name: Wire.read()
items.category_th: ไลบรารี Wire (I2C)
items.description_en: Reads a byte that was transmitted from a slave device to a master after a call to requestFrom() or was transmitted from a master to a slave. read() inherits from the Stream utility class.
items.parameters: none
items.returns: The next byte received
items.th: อ่านข้อมูลที่ขอมาทีละไบต์
items.micropython:
for b in data:
    print(b)
items.note_th: readfrom() ได้ข้อมูลทั้งหมดเป็น bytes

items.name: Wire.requestFrom()
items.category_th: ไลบรารี Wire (I2C)
items.description_en: Used by the master to request bytes from a slave device. The bytes may then be retrieved with the available() and read() functions. As of Arduino 1.0.1, requestFrom() accepts a boolean argument changing its behavior for compatibility with certain I2C devices. If true, requestFrom() sends a stop message after the request, releasing the I2C bus. If false, requestFrom() sends a restart message after the request. The bus will not be released, which prevents another master device from requesting between messages. This allows one master device to send multiple requests while in control. The default value is true.
items.parameters:
address: the 7-bit address of the device to request bytes from
quantity: the number of bytes to request
stop : boolean. true will send a stop message after the request, releasing the bus. false will continually send a restart after the request, keeping the connection active.
items.returns: None
items.th: ขอข้อมูลจากอุปกรณ์ I2C
items.micropython:
data = i2c.readfrom(0x68, 6)
data = i2c.readfrom_mem(0x68, 0x3B, 6)   # อ่านจากรีจิสเตอร์

items.name: Wire.write()
items.category_th: ไลบรารี Wire (I2C)
items.description_en: Writes data from a slave device in response to a request from a master, or queues bytes for transmission from a master to slave device (in-between calls to beginTransmission() and endTransmission()).
items.parameters:
value: a value to send as a single byte
string: a string to send as a series of bytes
data: an array of data to send as bytes
length: the number of bytes to transmit
items.returns: byte: write() will return the number of bytes written, though reading that number is optional
items.th: เขียนข้อมูลไปอุปกรณ์ I2C
items.micropython: i2c.writeto_mem(0x68, 0x6B, bytes([0]))   # เขียนรีจิสเตอร์ 0x6B

items.name: WireOnRequest
items.category_th: ไลบรารี Wire (I2C)
items.description_en: Register a function to be called when a master requests data from this slave device.
items.parameters: handler: the function to be called, takes no parameters and returns nothing, e.g.: void myHandler()
items.returns: None

items.name: SPI.begin()
items.category_th: ไลบรารี SPI
items.description_en: Initializes the SPI bus, setting SCK, MOSI, and SS to outputs, pulling SCK and MOSI low and SS high.
items.parameters: None
items.returns: None
items.th: เริ่มใช้ SPI
items.micropython: spi = SPI(1, baudrate=1000000, sck=Pin(18), mosi=Pin(23), miso=Pin(19))

items.name: SPI.end()
items.category_th: ไลบรารี SPI
items.description_en: Disables the SPI bus (leaving pin modes unchanged).
items.parameters: None
items.returns: None

items.name: SPI.setBitOrder()
items.category_th: ไลบรารี SPI
items.description_en: Sets the order of the bits shifted out of and into the SPI bus, either LSBFIRST (least-significant bit first) or MSBFIRST (most-significant bit first).
items.parameters: order: either LSBFIRST or MSBFIRST
items.returns: None

items.name: SPI.setClockDivider()
items.category_th: ไลบรารี SPI
items.description_en: Sets the SPI clock divider relative to the system clock. The dividers available are 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, or 128. The default setting is SPI_CLOCK_DIV4, which sets the SPI clock to one-quarter the frequency of the system clock.
items.parameters:
divider:
SPI_CLOCK_DIV2
SPI_CLOCK_DIV4
SPI_CLOCK_DIV8
SPI_CLOCK_DIV16
SPI_CLOCK_DIV32
SPI_CLOCK_DIV64 or
SPI_CLOCK_DIV128
items.returns: None

items.name: SPI.setDataMode()
items.category_th: ไลบรารี SPI
items.description_en: Sets the SPI data mode: that is, clock polarity and phase. See the Wikipedia article on SPI for details.
items.parameters: mode: SPI_MODE0, SPI_MODE1, SPI_MODE2, or SPI_MODE3
items.returns: None

items.name: SPI.transfer()
items.category_th: ไลบรารี SPI
items.description_en: Transfers one byte over the SPI bus, both sending and receiving.
items.parameters: val: the byte to send out over the bus
items.returns: the byte read from the bus
items.th: ส่งและรับข้อมูล SPI พร้อมกัน
items.micropython:
rx = bytearray(1)
cs.value(0)
spi.write_readinto(bytes([0x9F]), rx)
cs.value(1)
items.note_th: ต้องดึงขา CS เป็น 0 ก่อนส่งเอง

items.name: EEPROM.read()
items.category_th: ไลบรารี EEPROM
items.description_en: Reads a byte from the EEPROM. Locations that have never been written to have the value of 255.
items.parameters: address: the location to read from, starting from 0 (int)
items.returns: the value stored in that location (byte)
items.th: อ่านค่าจาก EEPROM
items.micropython:
with open('data.txt') as f:
    value = int(f.read())
items.note_th: เก็บเป็นไฟล์แทน

items.name: EEPROM.write()
items.category_th: ไลบรารี EEPROM
items.description_en: Write a byte to the EEPROM.
items.parameters:
address: the location to write to, starting from 0 (int)
value: the value to write, from 0 to 255 (byte)
items.returns: none
items.th: เขียนค่า 1 ไบต์ลง EEPROM
items.micropython:
with open('data.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write(str(value))
items.note_th: เก็บเป็นไฟล์แทน

items.name: file.available()
items.category_th: ไลบรารีการ์ด SD
items.description_en: Check if there are any bytes available for reading from the file. available() inherits from the Stream utility class.
items.parameters: file: an instance of the File class (returned by SD.open())
items.returns: the number of bytes available (int)

items.name: file.close()
items.category_th: ไลบรารีการ์ด SD
items.description_en: Close the file, and ensure that any data written to it is physically saved to the SD card.
items.parameters: file: an instance of the File class (returned by SD.open())
items.returns: none

items.name: file.flush()
items.category_th: ไลบรารีการ์ด SD
items.description_en: Ensures that any bytes written to the file are physically saved to the SD card. This is done automatically when the file is closed. flush() inherits from the Stream utility class.
items.parameters: file: an instance of the File class (returned by SD.open())
items.returns: none

items.name: file.isDirectory()
items.category_th: ไลบรารีการ์ด SD
items.description_en: Directories (or folders) are special kinds of files, this function reports if the current file is a directory or not.
items.parameters: file: an instance of the File class (returned by file.open()
items.returns: boolean

items.name: file.openNextFile()
items.category_th: ไลบรารีการ์ด SD
items.description_en: Reports the next file or folder in a directory.
items.parameters: file: an instance of the File class that is a directory
items.returns: char : the next file or folder in the path

items.name: file.peek()
items.category_th: ไลบรารีการ์ด SD
items.description_en: Read a byte from the file without advancing to the next one. That is, successive calls to peek() will return the same value, as will the next call to read(). peek() inherits from the Stream utility class.
items.parameters: file: an instance of the File class (returned by SD.open())
items.returns: The next byte (or character), or -1 if none is available.

items.name: file.position()
items.category_th: ไลบรารีการ์ด SD
items.description_en: Get the current position within the file (i.e. the location to which the next byte will be read from or written to).
items.parameters: file: an instance of the File class (returned by SD.open())
items.returns: the position within the file (unsigned long)

items.name: file.print()
items.category_th: ไลบรารีการ์ด SD
items.description_en: Print data to the file, which must have been opened for writing. Prints numbers as a sequence of digits, each an ASCII character (e.g. the number 123 is sent as the three characters '1', '2', '3').
items.parameters:
file: an instance of the File class (returned by SD.open())

items.th: ตัวเลข 1 ไบต์มี 8 บิต แต่ละบิตแทนขา 1 ขา: บิต 0 = 1, บิต 1 = 2, บิต 2 = 4 ... บิต 5 = 32, บิต 7 = 128 ค่า 32 เขียนเป็นเลขฐานสองคือ 00100000 เมื่อเอา value & 32 จะเหลือแค่บิตที่ 5 บิตอื่นหายหมด จึงใช้เช็กขาเดียวได้ 8 บิต เปิด/ปิดได้ 2 × 2 × ... × 2 = 2⁸ = 256 แบบ (0-255) พอร์ตขนานจึงส่งค่า 0-255

print((value >> 5) & 1)      # 1  -> อีกวิธี: เลื่อนบิตมาไว้ขวาสุด
print(bin(value))            # '0b10100001'

items.name: เลขคณิตมอดุโล: วนลำดับด้วย %
items.th: a % n คือเศษจากการหาร a ด้วย n ได้ค่า 0 ถึง n-1 เสมอ ใช้วนดัชนีของลำดับที่มี n ขั้น เช่น ลำดับสเต็ปมอเตอร์ 4 ขั้น: step = (step + 1) % 4 ไม่มีวันเกินขอบรายการ (โค้ดราวตากผ้าเดิมเช็ก if หลังบวกแล้ว จึงไปใช้ Step[4] ที่ไม่มีอยู่) ใช้กับเวลาได้ด้วย เช่น อีก 5 ชั่วโมงจาก 22 นาฬิกา = (22 + 5) % 24 = 3 นาฬิกา
items.micropython:
steps = [5, 6, 10, 9]
j = 0
for _ in range(10):
    print(steps[j])
    j = (j + 1) % 4          # เดินหน้า
# ถอยหลัง: j = (j - 1) % 4  (Python ให้ -1 % 4 = 3)
items.note_th: เทียบ MCS บทที่ 9.6-9.7 (เลขคณิตมอดุโลและเลขคณิตเศษ) ระวัง: ภาษา C ให้ -1 % 4 = -1 แต่ Python ให้ 3

items.th: ไฟฟ้าจะไหลได้ต้องมีเส้นทางครบรอบ: ออกจากขั้วบวกของแหล่งจ่าย ผ่านอุปกรณ์ (หลอดไฟ LED) แล้วกลับเข้าขั้วลบ ถ้าขาดตรงไหนแม้นิดเดียว ทั้งวงจรหยุดทำงาน กับบอร์ด: ขา OUTPUT คือขั้วบวก GND คือขั้วลบ LED ต้องมีตัวต้านทาน 220-330 Ω คั่นเสมอ

items.name: มอเตอร์และเครื่องกำเนิดไฟฟ้า
keywords: กำเนิดไฟฟ้า
items.th: มอเตอร์เปลี่ยนไฟฟ้าเป็นการหมุน โดยใช้แรงระหว่างแม่เหล็กถาวรกับแม่เหล็กไฟฟ้า กลับขั้วไฟ มอเตอร์หมุนกลับทาง ในทางกลับกัน ถ้าหมุนแกนมอเตอร์เอง จะได้ไฟฟ้าออกมา (ไดนาโมจักรยาน กังหันลม) บอร์ดคุมมอเตอร์ต้องผ่านวงจรขับ เช่น L298N หรือทรานซิสเตอร์ ห้ามต่อตรงกับขา

from machine import Pin, PWM
ena = PWM(Pin(25), freq=1000)
in1, in2 = Pin(26, Pin.OUT), Pin(27, Pin.OUT)
in1.value(1); in2.value(0)      # สลับ 0/1 = กลับทาง
ena.duty(600)                     # ความเร็ว 0-1023
